 Early voting gains support from both parties in Mississippi 
 Democrats and Republicans have called for a change to how the state handles voting 
 By Courtney Ann Jackson Published : Nov. 11, 2026 at 9:32 PM CST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - The election has raised questions about how Mississippi handles voting, and one potential change has support from both parties: early voting.
 Calls for early voting
 Brandon Presley, the 2023 Democratic nominee for governor, said Mississippi needs early voting.
 “We need early voting. 47 states in America have some form of early voting. That means there’s a lot of Republican states. Do we really think 47 states are wrong and we’re right? I think they’re probably on to something opening up their democracy,” Presley said.
 Scott Colom made similar comments in the days following the Senate race.
 “We need to do early voting. Listen, if you’re a Republican out there and you think you don’t want to do early voting because you’re scared of the results, you need to look yourself in the mirror and say, ‘There’s something wrong with my message,’” Colom said.
 Republican chairman comments on early voting
 Support for early voting is not limited to one party. The day before the election, Mississippi Republican Party Chairman Mike Hurst commented on absentee and early voting.
 “I think Republicans are starting to wake up and seeing that this absentee voting, this early voting here in Mississippi is a thing. It’s something they can and should do,” Hurst said.
 Current absentee voting rules
 Only voters with valid excuses can cast an absentee ballot early in Mississippi.
 Senate bill stalled in the House
 Sen. Jeremy England, R-Miss., the Senate Elections chairman, has sponsored legislation to change that for a couple of years.
 “Look, having election results available as soon as possible on election night is just a cleaner election. It gives people more confidence in the vote totals. And early voting would certainly give us quicker numbers,” England said.
 His proposal cleared the Senate but stalled in the House. England believes the bill would have met all the criteria for election security.
 “What the bill would have done is it would have allowed for 15 days, no-excuse in-person early voting at your circuit clerk’s office,” England said.
 England said he thinks Mississippi will eventually add no-excuse early voting, even if it does not happen in the next session.
